steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A food allergy is an immune system reaction to a specific food protein; symptoms can be severe and include anaphylaxis (a life-threatening reaction).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A food intolerance is a non-immune adverse reaction to food; symptoms are usually less severe and include bloating, diarrhoea, and stomach cramps.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition where gluten damages the small intestine lining, preventing nutrient absorption. Sufferers must follow a strict gluten-free diet.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Lactose intolerance is the inability to digest lactose (milk sugar) due to a lack of the enzyme lactase; symptoms include bloating and diarrhoea after consuming dairy.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the key difference between a food allergy and a food intolerance? | Q: What is coeliac disease and what diet must sufferers follow? | Q: Why does lactose intolerance cause symptoms after consuming dairy?

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always distinguish between allergy (immune, potentially fatal) and intolerance (non-immune, usually digestive) — this is a very common question. When adapting recipes, name the specific substitute ingredient AND explain why it works (e.g. 'gluten-free flour blend plus xanthan gum to replace the binding properties of gluten'). For vegan diets, always mention the key nutrients at risk: B12, iron, calcium, and omega-3 fatty acids. Learn the symptoms of coeliac disease, lactose intolerance, and anaphylaxis — they are frequently tested.
